scenes.narration: Hugging Face's Microduck is a 25-centimetre walking robot, under 800 grams. Its CEO says it's heading for about 20,000 preorders.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real close-up of a small bipedal hobby robot standing on a wooden desk next to a ruler, shallow depth of field, soft daylight
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: Fifteen motors, a camera, a depth sensor, and a beak that lifts about 100 grams. It walks, crouches, gets up after falls, and can even roller-skate.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real macro shot of small servo motors and circuit boards inside a hobby robot on a workbench, warm light
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: So how? Reinforcement learning in a physics simulator. Fall, retry, improve. Then the skill transfers to the real robot. That's sim-to-real.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real over-the-shoulder shot of a laptop screen showing an illustrative 3D physics simulation of many small robots falling and standing, dim office
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: At Nvidia GTC Berlin, four were demoed live. They stumbled and wandered. Real floors are hard.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real wide shot of small robots wobbling on a flat exhibition floor at a tech conference, onlookers' legs visible, bright event lighting
scenes.speaker: Arjun

scenes.narration: The software is open source. The hardware designs aren't, according to Pollen.
scenes.image_prompt: Photo-real close-up of source code on a monitor beside a closed hardware prototype on a desk, cool tones
scenes.speaker: Meera

scenes.narration: $399 before tax and shipping. New orders: about four to six months. A dev platform, not a toy.

scenes.speaker: Meera
